events.audience: Superintendents, Special Education Directors, Student Data Specialists
events.desc: Maine’s Essential Programs and Services (EPS) formula relies on staff full-time equivalency (FTE) data from each school year.
events.long:
Maine’s Essential Programs and Services (EPS) formula relies on staff full-time equivalency (FTE) data from each school year. This report is required to be certified by superintendents for state funding allocations to be calculated.

Signe Lynch, McKinney-Vento Homeless Education Specialist, will cover the foundational rights and resources available to assist students experiencing homelessness in accessing and succeeding in their school community.

Emergent Literacy Professional Learning (PLC) Communities are designed for preschool and kindergarten-level educators who are interested in learning more about children’s emergent literacy development between ages 3-6 and instructional practices to promote it.


Emergent literacy skills are the building blocks for learning to read and write.

events.desc: The Maine Department of Education (DOE) Offices of Teaching & Learning and Innovation are pleased to announce that registration is now open for EngageMEnt 2026–2027, a statewide…
events.long:
The Maine Department of Education (DOE) Offices of Teaching & Learning and Innovation are pleased to announce that registration is now open for EngageMEnt 2026–2027, a statewide professional learning opportunity designed to support educators in exploring innovative, engaging, and impactful practices for teaching and learning. Offered in partnership with the University of Maine at Orono and the University of Southern Maine, EngageMEnt creates opportunities for educators from across the state to learn, collaborate, reflect, and apply new ideas in their classrooms, schools, and communities.

The initiative also provides opportunities for practicing educators and preservice educators to learn alongside one another while exploring current educational priorities and practices. Building on the success of last year's implementation and participant feedback, EngageMEnt 2026–2027 has been designed as a year-long learning experience that supports both professional growth and implementation.

Rather than attending a single workshop, participants will join a cohort of educators who will continue learning together throughout the school year.

The Green Schools Peer Learning Workshops are an eight-part virtual series designed to help participants build long-term structures to advance sustainability in their school districts. Workshops will feature a brief presentation offering practical resources and real case studies from schools, followed by open time for participants to workshop their own sustainability initiatives.


Meetings will be facilitated by Ruth Poland and Micah Depper, two Maine teachers with experience shepherding school and district-level sustainability initiatives. The topics are sequential, but all are welcome to attend any session they are available. 


Sessions are designed to foster peer learning and build a supportive network of teachers, students, and administrators working to promote sustainability in their school buildings and practices. Registration is open to K-12 teachers, school administrators, district administrators, students, facilities managers, or any school community member seeking to advance sustainability in their district.

• The Attendance Data Corner: reviewing chronic absenteeism trends, statewide data, and seasonal considerations with proactive responses. • Voices from the Field: representing perspectives from early learning, elementary, middle, and high school, rural, suburban, and urban districts, alternative education programs, community partners, and family engagement organizations.
